paper.title: Contextual Safety Reasoning and Grounding for Open-World Robots
paper.central_claim: CORE: a VLM infers context-dependent safety predicates from visual observations online (no prior map or safety specification), a grounding module turns them into spatial safe sets/barrier functions via open-vocabulary segmentation and depth, and a control-barrier-function filter enforces them with probabilistic safety guarantees under perception uncertainty; in unseen environments it rivals an oracle with ground-truth context and significantly outperforms prior semantic safety methods that lack online contextual reasoning.
paper.claim_scope_note: Mobile robot navigation (Isaac Sim 60 evals; Boston Dynamics Spot 30 evals); open-weight Gemma 3 27B VLM; control-affine dynamics; guarantee conditional on a calibrated detection function.
paper.scope_note: Borderline scope: a B-class robot-safety layer (VLM + segmentation/depth tools + external CBF enforcement) around a nominal navigation controller; the VLM is an off-the-shelf open-weight model, not a frontier model, and there is no agent loop. Kept as reviewed; the controller may reverse this under the 2606.12372 scope precedent.

signatures.object: Safety constraint set for a navigating robot, inferred online instead of specified a priori; baseline = rules produced before deployment or geometry-only filter
signatures.information: RGB-D observation, odometry, high-level guidelines in the system prompt (role, five semantic classes, four spatial operators and rules); no map, no environment-specific rules, no oracle in CORE itself
signatures.operation: VLM (Gemma 3 27B, 4-bit) emits JSON of semantic classes and safe/unsafe predicates (ON/NEAR/AROUND/BETWEEN) with justification; open-vocabulary segmentation (SAM3) localizes classes; predicates become pixel sets, projected with depth into a 2D grid with safe/unsafe counts; thresholded at tau=0.5 into a safe set; signed-distance barrier; CBF-QP minimally modifies the nominal controller
signatures.output: Safe control input u_safe; barrier function h(x) updated online
signatures.conditions: Control-affine dynamics, metric depth, nominal controller agnostic, safe initialization (Assumption 1)
signatures.feedback: No feedback from the CBF back to the VLM; VLM re-queried on streaming frames; grid counts accumulate over observations
signatures.selection_rule_data: Fixed threshold on grid probability; no candidate selection; VLM model choice by predicate-prediction accuracy on 100 images from the experimental setup
signatures.persistence: Within-run accumulating grid counts only; nothing persists across runs
signatures.later_use: Barrier from accumulated grid used by the QP at each step
signatures.claimed_effect: Sim 95.0% total vs Oracle 98.3%, No Context 55.0%, Geometric 50.0%; hardware 86.6% vs Geometric 50.0%
signatures.failure_boundary: VLM misses a hazard at key timesteps (3.3%); depth-projection ghost obstacles; over-conservative VLM output; VLM latency 4.4 s; control-affine only

signatures.object: Probabilistic safe-traversal certificate for the online-constructed barrier
signatures.information: Detection probability function m(delta x) calibrated from VLM predicate accuracy; sensing radius; latency; speed
signatures.operation: Bound expected inverse distance to the nearest undetected unsafe region via supermartingale/Ville inequality; choose observations per traversal k*
signatures.output: Certificate P[exit safe set] <= delta (delta=0.1 found for c=1, l=0.1, k=3)
signatures.conditions: Assumption 1; independence of detection across contexts (gamma=0 used, admitted non-conservative); alpha held at 75% lower bound from 85% nominal
signatures.selection_rule_data: calibration from the 100-image Table II results
signatures.claimed_effect: 90% of trajectories safely traversed, conditional on the calibration
signatures.failure_boundary: no per-frame uncertainty; temporal correlation handled only by conservatism heuristics

retention_trace.explanation: Static pipeline plus in-run map accumulation; no learning, memory across episodes or harness revision is claimed. No retained-improvement claim is made or assessed.

gap.author_gap: Classical safety (CBF, HJ reachability, LTL) needs expert-written specifications and a priori environment knowledge; semantic-safety works still need a user to give precise rules for the specific environment, so the robot cannot reason about contextual safety itself.
gap.checked_gap: Real and specific (wet floor sign, cone lines, forklift buffers are context-dependent hazards a geometric filter cannot see). Nearest neighbours [10-12] (language-instructed safe sets/planners) and scene-graph LTL planners are cited and differentiated, but no neighbour is rerun or pinned in the package; the quantified residual (rivals oracle) rests on author-built baselines.
gap.lineage: CBF/HJ safety filters -> language-specified semantic safety (costmaps, reachability planners) -> VLM-proposed trajectories/grids -> CORE (VLM-inferred constraints + grounding + CBF with perception-uncertainty guarantee)

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Step 1 boundary: VLM confined to semantics/predicates, segmentation + depth + CBF-QP own exact geometry and enforcement (present). Step 2 typed, machine-checkable artifact: JSON of operator(class) predicates with a strict output format (present). Step 3 close the loop with solver-verifiable output: the CBF only consumes the artifact, no solver verdict returns to the VLM (absent). Step 4 ablate the structure: No Context / Geometric variants and offline prompt ablations (partly). Step 5 cost: module latency, memory, hardware reported (present).
matches.success_failure_checks: Success: boundary at comparative-advantage seam (met), typed artifacts (met), load-bearing mechanism ablated to a known baseline (partial: No Context), feedback signals obtainable at deployment (met). Failure: assembly of off-the-shelf parts (partial: Gemma, SAM3, CBF are off the shelf; the predicate/operator interface and certificate are the contribution), cost unmeasured (not present).
matches.reason: The operation actually executed is: learned model emits a typed spatial-predicate artifact that a sound solver (barrier/QP) enforces exactly. It differs from C25's feedback closure; sibling-less parent so no sibling contrast.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Identifies the load-bearing assumption of CBF safety (known, fixed barrier / safety spec) and relaxes it to an online, noisy-perception barrier with a re-derived probabilistic guarantee (Theorem 1). Tightness certificate, matching lower bound or characterization of when the weakened assumption holds is absent (calibration on 100 images, gamma=0 admitted non-conservative).
matches.success_failure_checks: Success: weaker condition shown to hold in the real setting (partial: only via calibration), prior methods fail precisely at the assumption (met: Geometric 0% unsafe). Failure: substitute equally strong or unverifiable condition (partly: independence/Assumption 1), under-differentiated from close precedent (partial).
matches.reason: A distinct operation (theory relaxation) from the system pipeline. No sub-card selected: C01/C05/C11/C19/C28/C29 concern attacks/defences, identifiability, selection rules, statistical certificates or distributed optimisation, not CBF-based robot safety.

domain_pattern.unassigned: Theorem 1 (probabilistic safe-traversal certificate under perception failure) and the CBF-QP enforcement have no domain card; no revision claimed from one paper.
revision_proposals: If more VLM-defined safety-filter papers appear, consider a candidate card 'VLM-defined safe set enforced by a barrier/QP filter outside the model' (needs at least two independent full texts; this paper alone is a case).

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Both put a non-learned checker outside the model; in CORE the learned model's artifact (predicates) defines what the external enforcer checks, so the correspondence is on the 'learned proposal -> sound external mechanism' structure.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: K201 gates a model proposal with feedback to the planner; CORE's filter modifies a nominal controller output and gives no feedback to the VLM. Differences keep the match partial.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Model emits a visual/semantic target that the harness back-projects with depth into metric space.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: K103 includes a feasibility check and a reselect loop; CORE has none and the artifact is a region set, not a target pose.

claims.text: CORE rivals an oracle with ground-truth context in unseen simulated environments.
claims.setting: Isaac Sim warehouse/hospital/outdoor, 12 tasks x 5 repeats, Gemma 3 27B
claims.selection_vs_test: VLM and calibration chosen on 100 images from the same setup
claims.allowed_conclusion: On these 12 designed scenarios CORE's total success is within ~3 points of the oracle-constraint version.

claims.text: Contextual reasoning is essential: far better than baselines without it.
claims.baseline_control: No Context (LLM rules before deployment), Geometric
claims.counterevidence: Baselines cannot see the scene or are blind to context by construction; not published prior methods
claims.allowed_conclusion: A pipeline with online VLM-inferred constraints beats the same pipeline with generic pre-deployment rules and with geometry only on these scenarios; not shown against published semantic safety systems.

claims.text: CORE transfers to a real Spot robot.
claims.setting: Lab space, 3 safe + 3 unsafe tasks x 5, DepthAnythingV3
claims.selection_vs_test: tasks not described; dev overlap unstated
claims.counterevidence: Attribution numbers inconsistent; trivial baseline; no Oracle/No Context on hardware
claims.allowed_conclusion: Works in one real lab setting for 6 tasks with 30 trials.

claims.text: Probabilistic safety guarantee under perception uncertainty (90% safe traversal).
claims.counterevidence: Non-conservative independence assumption admitted; no per-frame uncertainty
claims.allowed_conclusion: A conditional certificate whose validity rests on the calibration and independence assumptions; empirical ~93% on unsafe sim tasks is consistent but not an independent validation.

claims.text: Both safety logic and chain-of-thought matter for reasoning quality.
claims.selection_vs_test: offline, same set as VLM comparison
claims.result_denominator: No CoT: safe 61% vs 91%; no safety logic: unsafe 80% vs 85%
claims.counterevidence: No CI; offline not closed loop; safety-logic effect is small
claims.allowed_conclusion: CoT matters for safe-region prediction; safety-logic effect is a few points on 100 images.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop sim success plus 30 real-robot trials with counts on a physical Spot in a lab not described as used for construction; caveats: hardware baseline is trivial, hardware tasks undescribed, hyperparameters likely tuned in sim.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A frozen open-weight VLM that emits typed spatial safety predicates, grounded with segmentation and depth into a barrier enforced by a CBF-QP, prevented 93.3% of contextually unsafe designed tasks in 60 simulated trials (vs 16.6% for static generic rules, 0% for geometry only) at a 96.6% safe-task success, and prevented 86.6% of 15 unsafe tasks on a real Spot in 30 trials; the probabilistic guarantee is conditional on its calibration assumptions.
unresolved: Comparison with a published semantic safety method
Validity of the independence assumption behind the certificate
assessment.reproduction_note: All results are author-reported; nothing was run by us.

G.reason: Concrete, important bottleneck (rules must be supplied per environment; geometry misses contextual hazards) with neighbour lines cited and differentiated; residual bounded in Sec VI. Not 4 because neighbours [10-12] are not pinned/rerun and the headline superiority is against self-built baselines.

M.reason: Three-module chain with an explicit rationale for each (structured predicates, grounding to point-cloud grid, CBF) and a theorem linking detection accuracy to safe traversal; makes distinguishable predictions (Oracle vs No Context). Not 4 because the guarantee rests on assumptions the authors call non-conservative and acts at predicate-level accuracy, not per-frame.

X.reason: Prompt, operators, thresholds, dilation kernel, grid size, QP parameters, hardware, latency and failure modes are specified; limitations stated. Not 4 because the link from theorem to deployed settings is loose (k=3, gamma=0), hardware task details are missing and Table IV/text contain inconsistencies.

measurement.reason: Counts and stage-wise failure attribution exist (60 sim, 30 hardware), but the success predicate is only described informally (what counts as a violation, how hardware outcomes were judged) and hardware attribution percentages are inconsistent; anchor v2 caps undefined-criterion results at 2.

causality.reason: Same-pipeline baselines isolate online context reasoning, but No Context never sees the scene and Geometric cannot succeed by design, so the comparison is partly foregone; grounding, CBF and published methods are not tested; prompt ablations are offline only.

holdout.reason: Real Spot lab is a new embodiment/environment with retained gain over Geometric and no training in the method; but VLM selection and certificate calibration reuse images from the same setup as the sim evaluation, hardware tasks are undescribed and only the trivial baseline is run there.

statistics.reason: Five repeats per task and a failure breakdown, but no variance, CI or paired test, offline VLM tables on 100 images have no intervals, and Table IV percentages cannot arise from 30 trials.

cost.reason: Per-module latency, VLM latency and memory and hardware are disclosed; all baselines share the control synthesis; no per-episode cost aggregate and latency's role in the speed bound is only partly shown.

status.reason: Complete HTML full text with appendices read; scoped to B-class robot-safety harness (borderline: non-frontier open VLM, no agent loop) - scope flag recorded for controller/Opus.
